codingChallenge.solutionExample:
## State Architecture Review

### 1. Signal-based justification check:
Reviewed my Module 16 challenges - the Redux Toolkit slice (lesson 2)
and Zustand store (lesson 3) were both built because the lesson asked
for them, not because of a genuinely identified signal in a real
application. In a real project, I would need to confirm an actual
signal (lesson 1) before adopting either.

### 2. Category assignment check:
Confirmed my lesson 4 React Query implementation correctly handles
genuinely server-owned data (comments), with no server data
accidentally living in my lesson 2/3 client-state examples.

### 3. Local/Context scoping check:
My lesson 5 mixed-architecture example correctly keeps TaskCard's
expand state local and Auth state in Context, neither escalated
unnecessarily into the Zustand filter store.

### 4. Deliberate library choice check:
My lesson 5 example chose Zustand specifically because no signal
indicated a need for Redux's specific strengths (time-travel
debugging, ecosystem) - a deliberate, justified choice given the
scenario as described.

### 5. Periodic re-evaluation check:
This is the first time I've conducted this review on my own work
across this module - going forward, I would revisit any real
application's state architecture against these 5 checks quarterly.

## Migration plan:
1. In a real project, before adopting Redux Toolkit or Zustand, I would
   document the specific lesson-1 signal driving that decision, rather
   than building the store first and rationalizing afterward.
2. No genuine category mismatches were found in my own challenges,
   since each lesson's challenge was scoped to its own specific tool -
   but I would specifically watch for this in any real, evolved codebase.
validationRules: Must address all 5 checks from this lesson explicitly
Each finding must reference specific, concrete evidence (actual code, actual signals or their absence), not vague impressions
Must include at least one genuine finding representing a real gap, mismatch, or open question, not only confirmations that everything is already perfect
Must include a specific, concrete migration or process plan for at least 1-2 findings
hints: If reviewing your own Module 16 challenges, be honest that each tool was used because a lesson asked for it, not necessarily because a real, independent signal justified it - that's a legitimate, useful finding for check 1
For check 2 specifically, look hard for any case where server-fetched data ended up anywhere other than your React Query examples
Your migration plan should be concrete enough that you could actually act on it in a real project, not just a restatement of the finding

finalModuleProject.title: Architect A Complete Application's State, Then Defend Every Choice
finalModuleProject.goal: Synthesize everything from all 6 lessons — diagnostic signals, Redux Toolkit, Zustand, React Query, and deliberate multi-tool architecture — by building one complete application that genuinely requires all four state categories, then conducting lesson 6's full review against your own work with honest, evidence-based findings.
finalModuleProject.description: Build a small 'event planning' application: an events list fetched from a backend (server state), a single event card's own expand/collapse detail view (local state), authentication status needed across the header and an RSVP form (Context), and a frequently-changing, cross-component filter/sort panel for the events list (a client-state library of your choice, with justification). Use React Query for all server state, including a working mutation (RSVP submission) that correctly invalidates the events query. Conclude with a full, honest 5-check architectural review of your own implementation, following lesson 6's exact process, including at least one genuine finding and a fix.

requirements.requirement: Server state (the events list, and at least one mutation) managed entirely through React Query, never through useState/useEffect or a client-state library
At least one piece of genuinely local state (e.g. an event card's expand/collapse view) kept in plain useState, not lifted unnecessarily
Authentication/user state managed via Context, paired with a custom hook that throws a clear error when used outside its Provider
A frequently-changing, cross-component piece of state (filter/sort settings) managed via either Redux Toolkit or Zustand, with a written justification for the specific choice between them
A working mutation (e.g. RSVP submission) that correctly calls invalidateQueries on success, demonstrably keeping the events list in sync
A written, honest 5-check architectural review of this project's own implementation, including at least one genuine finding and a corresponding fix or migration plan

rubric.criterion: Server state is correctly and completely managed through React Query, with no category mismatches
Local state and Context are correctly scoped and appropriately used, not over- or under-escalated
The client-state library choice (Redux Toolkit or Zustand) is correctly implemented and deliberately, explicitly justified
The mutation-and-invalidation flow correctly keeps related data in sync
The final architectural review is thorough, honest, and demonstrates genuine evidence-based findings rather than unconditional self-approval

finalModuleProject.certificateUnlockCondition: Score 70 or above on the rubric and complete all 6 lesson coding challenges.
